beats: A Roman emperor once marched his army to the beach, to conquer the ocean!
According to the historian Suetonius, it happened in the year 40.
The emperor was Caligula, nicknamed Little Boots, and he badly wanted a war.
A runaway British prince surrendered, so he told the Senate Britain had submitted.
He lined up his legions on the coast of Gaul, catapults aimed at the waves.
He even sailed out a little way, then turned straight back.
Then came the order: pick up seashells!
The soldiers filled their helmets and their tunics.
He called them spoils of the sea, owed to Jupiter's temple and his own palace!
He built a lighthouse to mark the victory, and paid each man a hundred silver coins.
"Go away happy," he said. "Go away rich!"
Less than a year later, his own guards killed him.
The shells are long gone. But that lighthouse stood for sixteen centuries.
Then, in 1644, the cliff under it collapsed, and took the tower down.
So in the end, the ocean beat...
